author: Mark Atwood
text: RATIONALE CORRECTION 2026-05-12 (framing recalibration). The 2026-05-12 closure rationale included wrong-frame supporting arguments. Pulling those out for clarity; the underlying decision (A, pass-through Result) still holds on substantive grounds. STANDS (substantive): (1) framework-not-policy stance (AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5) -- a VerifyReport with structured findings would bake a finding taxonomy + severity model + rollup algorithm into framework-layer code, which is policy-shaped output. The workspace ships mechanisms; consumers compose their own report shapes by pattern-matching on the Error enum or wrapping ValidatedPath. (2) Result + Error is the Rust-idiomatic shape for 'verify-or-fail' verdicts; new identity-binding failure modes ride as new Error variants. (3) ValidatedPath already exposes §6.1.5 wrap-up outputs for success-side detail. WITHDRAWN (wrong-frame): (4) 'Door stays open: a future verify_*_verbose(...) -> VerifyReport can be added on concrete consumer demand' -- this is post-launch YAGNI reasoning. In a prelaunch design phase, 'we can add it later' is not a tiebreaker; the decision should rest on whether the structured-findings shape is part of the right design. Substantive answer: it isn't, because framework-not-policy says findings taxonomy is the consumer's job. ALSO: the original closure comment cited 'same logic that demoted OSCAL and abandoned zlint mirroring applies.' That citation should be narrowed: the OSCAL demotion had a substantive reason (compliance-vocabulary vs rule-predicate-DSL); the zlint-mirroring abandonment's rationale was partly wrong-framed and is itself under correction. Citing them as transitive precedent is unreliable. The framework-not-policy argument stands on its own without precedent.
